findings.title: Shared default timestamp evaluated at import time
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, AssignmentSource declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. The default is evaluated once at import, so every AssignmentSource created via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued shares the same timestamp. Someone reading only this finding should understand: all inbound assignments get identical queued times, making the field useless for ordering, debugging, or any future debounce logic. Fix with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Raw datetime in Celery payload breaks serialization round-trip
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py to_dict uses asdict and returns a raw datetime for queued, and src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py passes that dict as assignment_source_dict to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime object either fails to enqueue or arrives as an ISO string. from_dict then does cls(**input_dict) with no string-to-datetime parsing and only catches ValueError/TypeError, so a string queued silently creates an object with queued as str or fails. Consequence: inbound-originated outbound syncs that now carry a source can fail to serialize or lose type instead of being cleanly filtered.

findings.title: Malformed source fails open and re-creates sync loop
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py lines 53-56, AssignmentSource.from_dict returning None on bad input is treated the same as no source, then installation.should_sync is called with None which returns True if outbound sync is enabled. A malformed or type-mismatched assignment_source_dict therefore propagates the update instead of suppressing it. Consequence: the exact Jira rapid-reassign loop this PR claims to fix can still occur when the payload is corrupted or has unexpected types, failing open instead of failing closed or logging.
